55% of all study notifications reviewed by regulatory authorities are valid according to their criteria.

55% of clinical drug study documents submitted to the regulatory agency in 1992, in 1994, in 1996 and in 1998 were valid, and that 71% of studies approved by two university hospital ethics committees were notified to the authority before commencement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validity of clinical study notifications reviewed by regulatory agencies and the reporting of clinical drug study results.
the quality of the clinical study notifications reviewed by a national authority.
the quality of the notifications and the validity of the decisions made by the regulatory agency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of clinical drug study notification reviewed by the regulatory authority in Finland is good, but there is still room for improvement.
the regulatory agency in practice has not been able to guarantee the safety of subjects participating in clinical studies in Finland.
the quality of the study notifications is not satisfactory, which may be a result of the current division of responsibilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulatory agency in question is doing its job well and that the clinical research community should do a better job in complying with regulatory requirements.
the quality of study documents is not good enough to ensure the quality of the clinical trials.
the regulatory agencies and ethics committees should improve their current work practices by a more precise division of responsibilities and by better compliance with regulatory guidelines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulatory authorities should have a better overview of the clinical studies being carried out in Finland.
the regulatory authorities should have more influence on clinical research in their own country.
the regulatory agency in question should be notified of all studies planned in Finland, and the agency should be more active in following the progress of the studies.
